prerequisites: Basic training modules (common to industrial branch and specific to Industrial Electronic and Automatic Engineering)

learning_outcomes.text: Select an appropriate sensor for common industrial measurements: flow, pressure, etc., within the context of the control system (RII-1).
Design the complete basic measurement system for the most common industrial measurements and integrate it into the control system (RII-2).
Select and configure a specific data acquisition system (RII-3).
Distinguish possible sources of interference and act on instrumentation systems to avoid their effect (RII-4).
Connect different measurement instruments through an instrumentation bus (RII-5).

syllabus_topics: Measurement of the main industrial magnitudes
Presence and proximity detection. Measurement of position, speed, acceleration and vibration
Signal conditioning, acquisition, processing and transmission
General review of signal conditioning systems
Signal transmission systems via cable: voltage and current loops
Shielded enclosures for harsh industrial environments
Considerations in the design of PCBs for instrumentation
Types of DASs for monitoring and control

assessment_methods.method: Active participation in the teaching process (questions and issues during classes, attendance at tutorials, follow-up of assignments)

Practical assignments on course subjects (group work on the general content of the course, consisting of the complete design of a data acquisition system from sensors and the visualization/storage of values in some type of computer support)

assessment_rules: For ordinary calls, the final grade is based on 20% active participation, 30% practical assignments, and 50% theoretical exam. For extraordinary calls, the assessment consists of a theoretical exam (75%) and a practical exam (25%). Differential evaluation uses a single exam covering the entire course.
bibliography: "Instrumentación electrónica. 230 problemas resueltos", M.A. Pérez. Ed. Garceta. 2012

Pcb.com website with recommendations for PCB design for instrumental systems
